EE04.why: Also a one-variable linear equation with fractions and x on both sides ((x − 4)/3 = (x + 2)/5), but that one is a proportion of binomials solved by cross-multiplying. EE04 has fractional coefficients plus constants, so it is cleared with the LCD 4. Same skill, different setup.

EE05.why: Same asked quantity (the equation of a vertical line), the same point (3, −2) and the same answer x = 3. ACT-647 signals the vertical line with a second point (3, 5) and EE05 says 'undefined slope', but the reasoning and the result are the same.

EE20.why: Same setup: a road rises 3 m over a horizontal distance of 40 m and asks about the angle with the horizontal. ACT-730 asks for an inverse-tangent expression and EE20 asks for the tangent value (rise/run). The core step is the same, but the asked quantity is different.
A road rises 120 ft over 2,400 ft, and the asked quantity is rise/run as a percent grade. The arithmetic is the same as EE20's tan = 3/20, framed as a grade rather than as trigonometry.

EE34.why: Same two-case procedure for |ax − b| = c. ACT-597 asks for the solution set of |x − 3| = 5 and EE34 asks for the sum of the solutions of |2x − 3| = 7. The asked quantity and the coefficient differ.
